turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, I know you're probably very busy. 

I just came in because... well, I guess I've been struggling a little bit lately. It's probably silly, and I'm sure other people have it much worse, but I just can't stop feeling like every little thing that goes wrong is my fault. Like I'm just a really bad employee right now, and a bad homeowner, too. I just have this heavy feeling that I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. 

Is that... does that make sense? I'm sorry if it sounds like I'm just complaining, I just didn't really know where else to go.

symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient explicitly states they feel everything that goes wrong is their fault, view themselves as a bad employee and homeowner, and feel they deserve to lose everything they have worked for.

turns.doctor_question: During these past two years, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep?
turns.patient_response:
Um... well, my sleep has been a little off, but I'm sure that's just because I worry too much about work. But my appetite... it's kind of been all over the place, I guess.

I know I should be taking better care of myself, and I feel really guilty about it. I'm trying to do better, I promise. Is it... is it okay that I just eat toast sometimes? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm completely falling apart.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned feeling like a bad employee and homeowner; do you often feel a sense of low self-esteem or inadequacy in your daily life?
turns.patient_response:
Um... yeah, I guess I do. It's actually kind of the main reason I finally decided to come in and see someone. I just... I can't seem to stop feeling like every little thing that goes wrong is completely my fault. 

Like at work, if a project gets delayed, or at home if something breaks... I just immediately feel like I'm a terrible employee and a really bad homeowner. It's this awful feeling that I just... I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for because I'm just not good enough. 

I know it probably sounds silly, and I really try to remind myself of the good things I've done, but it's just so hard to shake that feeling. I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself. Is it... is it normal to feel that guilty all the time? I hope I don't sound like I'm just throwing a pity party... I really am trying to be better about it.

turns.doctor_question: During these past two years, have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where your mood was so low that you felt almost completely unable to function or perform your daily tasks?
turns.patient_response:
Um... well... I wouldn't say I was completely unable to function. I mean, I'm still going to work every day, I promise. I really try not to let things completely fall apart. 

But... I guess there have been times, definitely more than a couple of weeks, where it just takes so much effort to do even the basic stuff. Like, I've had to cancel on friends a few times because I just couldn't face going out, and... my townhouse has gotten a lot messier than I usually let it. I feel terrible about that. 

And at work... I've made a few mistakes. Nothing huge, but enough that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to check in on my performance. I felt so awful about it, I really did. I'm trying so hard to keep up, it just... it takes everything I have right now. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't mean I'm doing a terrible job at everything. I really am trying my best to keep it all together.

turns.doctor_question: During these two years, were there any specific two-week periods where you felt significantly worse than your usual 'low' baseline, such as feeling completely hopeless, having almost no energy to get out of bed, or having recurring thoughts that life wasn't worth living?
turns.patient_response:
Um... well, no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely haven't felt like life wasn't worth living or anything like that, I promise. I know how serious that is, and I would never want to do anything to hurt myself or worry anyone. 

There are definitely days where getting out of bed feels... a little harder than it probably should, and maybe I feel a bit more tired than usual. But I always push through it, you know? I always manage to get up and go to work. I wouldn't say I've ever been completely hopeless for two whole weeks straight. 

I really try to look on the bright side and keep pushing forward, even when it's tough. Is it okay that I just feel really tired sometimes? I hope that doesn't mean I'm failing at managing things... I'm really trying to stay positive.
